plugin.ssh.description: An ssh agent: the vault’s keys sign without ever reaching the disk
plugin.ssh.title: Routes
routes.empty.body: Pick an SSH key and list its hosts, comma separated — for example *.example.net, gitlab.example.com. From then on ssh gets exactly that key and nothing else.
routes.empty.title: No host is bound to a key yet
routes.title: Host → key
settings.sshAgentHint: A disabled agent behaves as an absent one: ssh falls back to key files.
settings.sshAskHint: Confirmation is asked via Touch ID.
settings.sshConfigHint: At the end of the file, and nowhere else: ssh reads it top to bottom, and %h in Match exec is whatever is known by that line. Above the Host blocks that is the alias you typed ("vps"), not the host name, and no route is found. The path is absolute on purpose: Match exec runs through /bin/sh, where PATH differs.
settings.sshSocketHint: One socket with every key — for IDEs and git clients that ignore ssh_config. ssh will try keys one by one, as with a regular agent.
settings.sshSocketPathHint: Add the line to ~/.zshrc or the app's settings. The socket lives while the vault is unlocked.
sshkey.importHint: A new Ed25519 key is made for you. To use your own, copy its private key (OpenSSH or RSA in PEM) and press “Import from clipboard”: it is checked at once.
sshkey.passphraseHint: Used once to open the key; it is not stored.
sshkey.privateStored: The private key stays in the vault and is never shown here: the agent signs with it without it reaching the disk.
sshkey.regenerateHint: A new pair replaces this one on save. Servers that have the old public key in authorized_keys will stop letting it in until the new one is put there.
sshkey.replaceHint: Copy a private key you already have and import it from the clipboard; it is checked first. The old key stops working wherever only it was trusted.
sshkey.replacingWarn: On save the current key is replaced for good: servers that trust only the old public key will stop letting you in.
